author: desk
note: Desk-written plain-English summary, not a tiered fact. Written to help a reader understand the business quickly; verify any figure against the fact store before using it in a report.
one_liner: Makes ChatGPT and sells the AI models behind it.
what_it_does: OpenAI builds large AI models and sells them both directly to consumers through ChatGPT and to developers and businesses through an interface. It has the largest consumer footprint of any AI company and an unusual corporate structure created when a nonprofit added a commercial arm.
how_it_makes_money: Consumer subscriptions to ChatGPT, business and enterprise plans, and usage-based developer charges. The consumer share is far larger than at any other frontier lab.
why_it_matters: It sets the pace, the pricing and the public expectations for the whole category. Its numbers are the benchmark others are measured against, which makes the reporting differences below important.
competitive_position: Competes with Anthropic, Google and Meta at the frontier, and with a widening field of cheaper open-weight models underneath.
key_risks: Corporate structure and governance remain unusual and have been contested before.
Consumer revenue is less durable than enterprise revenue if a competitor ships something better.
Compute commitments are very large and long-dated.
Reports revenue net, so headline comparisons against gross-reporting rivals overstate the gap.

glossary.definition: Revenue after payments to partners are deducted. A net figure looks smaller than a gross one for identical business.
An arrangement where investor returns are limited above a threshold, with the remainder going to the controlling nonprofit.
